Brilliant job! You are really getting the hang of this. 

For one-quarter plus one-eighth, the denominators are four and eight, which are different. Can you find a way to change one-quarter so it has a denominator of eight, just like we did in your very first question?
um, is it 2/12? i just added the top numbers and the bottom numbers together, but im not really sure if thats right.

That is a super common thing to try, but adding the denominators together doesn't quite work here. 

Remember, we need the bottom numbers to be the same before we can add. Can you use what you learned in the very first question to change one-quarter so its denominator is eight?
